writeup.headline: Leidos rates Hold: low valuation offset by weak share-price trend and modest growth ahead of Q3 results.
writeup.thesis: Leidos scores 57, a Hold, with valuation the clear strength at a factor score of 93. In absolute terms the multiples are low, at 1.0x sales, 8.1x free cash flow and 11.2x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 7.4 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. The stock is also cheap against its own history, with P/FCF cheaper than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends and EV/EBIT cheaper than at 56 of the last 61 month-ends. Holding the score back are a weak trend (32), with shares down 34.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and the price 30.0% below its 52-week high, plus middling growth (49) on TTM revenue growth of 3.5%, though latest-quarter revenue growth of 7.4% year on year shows growth sped up by 3.8 pp. Quality is moderate at 58, with a 12.3% FCF margin and diluted share count down 3.1% year on year. The balance sheet scores 44, with net debt at 2.44x FCF and cash covering 0.12 of debt.
key_risks: Health segment margin pressure, which prompted a JPMorgan downgrade and several price-target cuts in October
MHS GENESIS bridge contract scope shrinking as work moves to other contractors
Persistent share-price weakness, with shares 12.7 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days
Leverage, with net debt at 2.44x FCF and a low cash-to-debt ratio of 0.12
Thin 17.5% gross margin typical of government services leaves little room for cost overruns
what_would_change: A rise of 8 points to 65 would lift the rating to Buy, most plausibly from a recovering trend score or stronger growth if Q3 results on 2026-11-03 confirm the acceleration
